readings.evidence: In maariv-s22-top-l.png, line 1, the word comes after וְאַחֲרֵי. Under the ע there is a tsere with a short vertical stroke right next to it, which I read as a meteg/gaya on the ע (medium confidence at this resolution). The נ has a tsere and the כ has a segol. A single dot sits above the כ. Higher up, in the space between lines, there is a separate mark of three stacked dots (⋮) above the כ/ם area. I did not see a printed zakef in its usual form: the single dot over the כ may be this book's stress or pause sign, or a weakly printed accent. I am reporting it as printed and not filling it in from the standard Torah text.

In maariv-s22-top-r.png, line 3, the word ends the verse after קְדֹשִׁים. The ל has a tsere, and I see a small vertical stroke beside it, which I read as meteg/gaya on the ל (medium-to-low confidence). The holam dot is at the upper left of the ל, next to the א, and the א itself is unpointed. The ה has a tsere. Under the כ there is a segol with a clear vertical stroke, the silluq (high confidence), followed by sof pasuq ׃.

In maariv-s22-top-l.png, line 3, the phrase reads אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר, with a double-stroke accent above the נ of אֲנִי. The א has a hataf segol, and I see what looks like a vertical stroke beside it, which I read tentatively as meteg/gaya (low-to-medium confidence). The holam dot is above the ל on the left side, the ה has a tsere, and the כ has a segol. A single dot sits above the כ, as in עיניכם, but there is no ⋮ above this word. There is no silluq, which fits a word in mid-verse.

readings.text: יש לגרוס אלהיכם לאמת, אכן יתן רוח מעט שלא יבולע הא׳
readings.evidence: The rubric is printed in a cursive-style font in which א looks like ח, as in חלהיכס = אלהיכם and לחמת = לאמת. The first letter of the disputed word is that same א shape and has no tall ascender. By contrast, the ל in לחמת and in לגרוס has the clear tall ascender. So the word is אכן, not לכן (high confidence).
